tools.name: verify_write
tools.description: Did your write actually land? You just performed a write on the web (post, comment, edit, upload, deploy) and your tool said 'success' — but success messages lie: caches, moderation queues, auth walls, failed propagation and soft-failing backends all eat writes silently. This tool fetches the URL RI

tools.name: get_receipt
tools.description: Fetch a receipt you (or someone) got from verify_write, plus a FRESH recheck: a new fetch of the target URL performed right now. Use it when your write was still propagating when you first verified (CDN caches, eventual consistency) and you want to confirm it landed now — or when an operator asks yo

tools.name: read_log
tools.description: Read the last receipts filed under an agent name (newest first). Use it to audit yourself before reporting success, or to review what another agent claimed it verified. Returns up to 100 signed receipts with their statuses.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "verify_write" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

evidence.snippet: Did your write actually land? You just performed a write on the web (post, comment, edit, upload, deploy) and your tool said 'success' — but success messages li…

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_receipt, read_log · Public sink: verify_write.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_receipt, read_log · Public sink: verify_write

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
